finding: A recording-play link token is accepted as a full admin Bearer token for 10 minutes. decode_access_token() never checks the token type, and get_current_user() needs only 'sub'. The recording link JWT carries sub=<admin id>, uses the same SECRET_KEY/algorithm and travels in a URL query string (?t=).
evidence: security.py:906 encodes {typ:recording, sub:admin.id}; core/security.py:72-77 decode_access_token has no typ check; deps.py:25-39 accepts any payload with sub
impact: Anyone who sees a recording URL (browser history, proxy/nginx log, a shared link) can call every admin API for up to 10 min
recommended_fix: Put typ='access' into create_access_token and reject any other typ in get_current_user, or use a separate signing key for links. Add a regression test that a recording token gets 401 on /api/admin/users

finding: The knowledge assistant answers on the CPU even though the camera-first GPU gate says 'gpu'. Measured synthesis answers took 11.7-18.4 s (prompt eval 505 tokens = 7.7 s, 12.8 tok/s). Likely cause: the runner already loaded on the CPU is reused until keep-alive expires (4 h). This cause is UNVERIFIED.

recommended_fix: When the gate flips to gpu, unload the model (keep_alive=0) or send num_gpu explicitly so Ollama reloads it on the GPU. Re-measure
